opti-1: Long ago, posters invited people to see America's national parks.
opti-2: In 1947, the Everglades became a national park.
opti-3: Yellowstone was the very first, back in 1872.
opti-4: Each park has its own weather, land, and living things.
opti-5: Scientists study each park, then share what they find.
opti-6: How do scientists figure out which organisms belong in a habitat, and why does protecting that habitat matter?
32-01-welcome: Our film starts with old national park posters and stamps. First, inspect a small mystery cone.
32-01-lesson: Today you're an ecologist. Watch wolves come home, run the Winter Test, then stamp your Park Passport.
32-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
32-01-assign: Time to show what you learned. Pick a park, then draw its ecosystem with one connection arrow.
how-32-01-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the cone, then tap three things you notice.
how-32-01-compare: Put the deep snow under one tray and the lower valley under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Start winter. Then swap.
how-32-01-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing stamp: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-32-01-det: Pick three cards, one at a time. Tap a feature that helps it survive, then name its home park. Predict if it could survive in a different park, and see the evidence.
how-32-01-partc: Draw a simple ecosystem scene from the park you picked. Show at least four organisms in their habitat. Label each organism, and draw one arrow showing how one thing connects to another (like wolf → elk).
